name: Bundledocs
tagline: Cloud software that compiles paginated, indexed, hyperlinked document bundles for legal and insurance work.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Bundledocs sells per-user subscriptions via quote, so no public number is safe to print.

verdictSummary: The mechanical core of bundling is not mysterious: merge PDFs in a defined order, stamp sequential page numbers, build a table of contents, and hyperlink the index entries to the right pages. An agent can do all of that with pikepdf and reportlab in an afternoon, and for one person preparing their own bundles it will genuinely work. What it will not do on day one is swallow .msg emails, Excel sheets, HEICs and scanned faxes and turn them into clean paginated PDFs, which is most of the actual labour in real matters. It also will not know your jurisdiction's pagination and indexing conventions, and it will not have anyone to blame when a bundle gets bounced the morning of a hearing. Build it if you are bundling your own documents; keep the subscription if a court or an insurer is on the receiving end.
coreLoopDIY: Point a script at a folder of PDFs plus an ordering file and get back a single bundle with continuous page numbering, PDF bookmarks, and a hyperlinked index page.
requirements: Python 3.11 with pikepdf, pypdf and reportlab
LibreOffice installed if you want DOCX and XLSX conversion
Optional: Tesseract and ocrmypdf for scanned input
Local disk space; large bundles get big fast
whatYouLose: Native format handling for the messy stuff: Outlook .msg, embedded attachments, spreadsheets that must not be clipped at the page edge
Reliable OCR and page cleanup on scanned exhibits
Jurisdiction and client specific pagination, index and stamping profiles that someone else maintains when rules change
Shared bundles, version control and multiple people working one matter at once
A support line and an audit trail when a bundle is rejected under deadline
moatNotes: The moat is less the PDF plumbing and more the input funnel: DMS connectors, email formats, and the accumulated knowledge of what each court will accept.
whyPeopleStillPay: Bundling is deadline work with asymmetric downside. The cost of a subscription is noise next to one hearing where the index pagination is off by two pages and a judge says so out loud. Firms also pay for the boring input side: pulling from iManage or SharePoint, converting email threads with attachments intact, and reproducing the same house style every time without a paralegal babysitting a script. A personal build removes the licence fee and keeps the liability, which is a fine trade for your own documents and a bad one for a client's.
notes: The merge-and-paginate part is a weekend; the input funnel is the product.
prompt:
Build a local command line tool called "bundle" that compiles a paginated, indexed PDF bundle from a folder of documents.

Stack: Python 3.11, pikepdf for PDF manipulation, pypdf for page counts, reportlab for generated index and cover pages, click for the CLI, PyYAML for config. No web server, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud calls.

Input: a working directory containing a bundle.yaml file. bundle.yaml defines bundle title, case reference, numbering style (arabic, prefixed like "A-1", or per-section restart), and an ordered list of sections, each with a name and an ordered list of file paths with optional display titles and dates.

Behaviour:
1. Validate that every listed file exists and is readable; fail loudly with the full list of problems before doing any work.
2. Convert non-PDF inputs to PDF by shelling out to headless LibreOffice for doc, docx, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx, txt, and to img2pdf or Pillow for png, jpg, jpeg, tif. If LibreOffice is missing, skip those files and report them clearly rather than crashing.
3. Merge everything in declared order into one output PDF.
4. Stamp page numbers in the bottom right of every page using the configured numbering style, drawn on an overlay so the original content is never rewritten.
5. Generate a cover page and an index listing section names, document titles, dates and start page numbers.
6. Add internal PDF link annotations from each index row to the first page of that document, and build a matching PDF bookmark tree with sections as parents.
7. Write output to ./out/bundle.pdf plus ./out/index.csv with one row per document: section, title, date, start page, end page, source filename.

Also implement "bundle init" to scaffold a bundle.yaml from the files currently in the folder, sorted by name, so the user edits rather than types from scratch.

Explicitly out of scope: OCR, redaction, collaboration, DMS connectors, .msg email parsing, and any GUI. Note those as unimplemented in the README.

Include a README with install steps, a sample bundle.yaml, and pytest tests covering numbering continuity, index page offsets after the index itself grows past one page, and missing file handling. Keep any configurable paths in .env, not hardcoded.
